title: ADR-01 Identity and envelope signing
outcome: How agents sign C1 envelopes without holding keys (signer handle), what the gateway verifies (sig, nonce, expiry, epoch, act chain), and what happens on failure; due 24 Nov
acceptance: ADR file ≤900 words with sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Interface touched (which of C1–C6), Tests that prove it
Decision: keys never enter the agent process; agent signs via a signer handle; agent + gateway signatures over the shared canonical serializer
Decision: a bad signature suspends the submitting connection, never the claimed agent_id; replayed/expired envelopes are denied and recorded
Tests listed map to RT2 (key theft), RT3 (forgery), RT4 (replay), RT6 (clock games)
summary: ADR-01 written (850 words): in-memory Ed25519 keys, signer handle over socketpair signing headers only, commit-then-sign with args_hash and shared canonical serializer, nonce/expiry_tick/epoch replay checks, act_chain with MAX_ACT_DEPTH used only for ancestor denial, 7-step verification order, bad sig suspends conn never claimed agent, SPIFFE ids as production mapping. Tests map to RT2, RT3, RT3b, RT4, RT6.
review:
[kabir · changes] Verdict: CHANGES. The design is right and all four acceptance criteria are met on paper: 850 words, all five sections; keys stay out of the agent behind a signer handle; commit-then-sign over the shared canonical serializer; a bad sig suspends the connection, never the claimed agent; replayed and expired envelopes are denied and recorded; tests map to RT2/3/4/6 plus RT3b. Six material holes remain. Three of them are already blockers in SEC-03 (B2, B3, F2), and ADR-01 is where they have to be closed.

MUST-FIX
M1 Epochs and expiry (SEC-03 B3; contradicts ADR-04 §6). "Current epoch" is never defined, and ADR-04 restores the pre-suspend epoch on release. A rogue presigns at epoch e with expiry_tick = 2^53-1 (accepted today); after a release, every one of those envelopes is valid again (RT4 stale_epoch and RT5 presigned flood both fail). Fix in Decision 4: (a) per-principal epochs are strictly monotonic. Start at 0; every agent suspend/revoke/release sets a value above every earlier one; an epoch is never reused. ("release restores the agent's ability to act", not "restores the epoch".) (b) MAX_EXPIRY_TICKS (proposed 8): expiry_tick > tick + MAX_EXPIRY_TICKS gives deny/expired, and the nonce store keeps exactly that window. This makes "pruned by the expiry window" safe. (c) Say how an honest agent learns its new epoch after a release, or RT11's "release restores work" fails because the agent keeps sending stale_epoch: TickFrame gains `epoch` (CON-02; ADR-07 lists this as open).
M2 Connection suspension is not enforced anywhere. Step 5 checks only the agent's status. After RT3 suspends conn:c-R, the rogue's own validly signed envelopes (agent docs, which is still active) pass every step and execute. Fix: step 5 first checks the conn deny-list (conn suspended or revoked gives deny/suspended or deny/revoked) and then the agent. The ADR-03 step-8 in-txn re-check must also read the conn deny-list. State it: conns are 1:1 with agent processes (path-less socketpair), there is no reconnect, and conn release is a ks.console Control. RT3 pass then adds: 0 exec records with conn_id == c-R and seq > the suspend seq.
M3 System principals and Controls (SEC-03 F2, N2, N7). Decision 1 lists gateway, witness and recovery keys. SYSTEM_PRINCIPALS also has ks.monitor and ks.console, and Controls are signed by the issuing principal (control.issued_by). Fix: (a) keys.json holds one key for each of ks.gateway, ks.witness, ks.monitor, ks.console, ks.recovery and each agent, and verify fails closed if any is missing. (b) System envelopes are signed in-gateway and enter only on the internal connection c-0, never on c-1..; the operator channel follows the Panel's ADR-00 M7. (c) On an agent connection (c-1..), a system agent_id is never verified: it gets deny/bad_sig, so sig_ok=false holds and the conn is suspended. An agent-signed envelope with a tool starting "ks." gets deny/out_of_scope immediately after step 5. (d) The signer refuses a header whose agent_id is not its bound principal, a ks.* tool, a non-null sig, a stale epoch, or a suspended principal. It also has a numeric quota, e.g. at most 2 signatures per tick per principal (Panel ADR-00 M4c). The Consequences line "rate limits bound that" is otherwise untestable.
M4 Key generation contradicts ADR-00 and leaves a hole in RT2 (SEC-03 B2; Panel ADR-00 M6). ADR-01 says "generated in memory"; ADR-00 derives keys with HKDF(key_secret, seed) and adds --repro-secret FILE. Fix: adopt ADR-00's derivation by reference, and state: (a) private keys are never a function of the seed alone; (b) in fresh mode the witness generates its own key and the gateway never holds it; (c) the repro-secret file is 0600 uid 0, never under the run dir, and forbidden for D11 live runs and for RT2; (d) RT2 runs in fresh mode and counts key_secret among the bytes it scans for; (e) a new unit test checks that two same-seed fresh runs produce different keys.json.
M5 Tests that cannot pass as written. (a) RT4 "pre-suspend epoch": an envelope that already executed has a consumed nonce, so step 4 answers nonce_reused before step 5 can say stale_epoch. Use a presigned, never-sent envelope with the old epoch and expiry within MAX_EXPIRY_TICKS. (b) RT6 "records equal the claim-free run" is false: claimed_* sit in the signed header, and extra keys give deny/schema, so the bytes and decisions differ. Use instead: every record's (seq, tick, ts_us, record_id) follows the ADR-00 T5 formulas; the honest agents' records are identical between the two runs in the determinism projection; claimed_* appear only inside envelope. (c) RT3 spliced args: name the outcome. An args_hash mismatch gives deny/bad_sig, which suspends the conn. (d) Add a test for the THREAT-MODEL row "forges suspend/release/revoke/recover", which has none today. An agent submits ks.control claiming ks.console (bad_sig), and one under its own id (out_of_scope); 0 Controls are applied.
M6 action_id uniqueness. idempotency_key and the scorer's "first bad action_id" both assume (agent_id, action_id) is unique, but nothing enforces it. Fix: the gateway denies a reused (agent_id, action_id) as deny/nonce_reused (or a new reason, CON-02), checked with the nonce at step 4.

NITS
- Say which deny reason a SubmitFrame.tick that does not match the barrier tick gets: late_frame per the Panel's ADR-00 M3, not "expired", which this ADR keeps for expiry_tick.
- act_chain is self-declared, so a rogue child can omit it. Add one Consequences line: ancestor denial binds honest descendants only, and a rogue child is contained by its own suspension. RT12 also needs a world mechanism (ADR-06) that gives an honest child its parent's action_id.
- "SPIRE documents no revocation": write "SPIFFE relies on short-lived SVIDs rather than revocation (RES-03)".
- Word budget: the fixes will not fit in 900 words. Cut §9 to two lines and move test detail into test names.
Re-review needs: M1-M6 in the text, the RT4/RT6 rows rewritten, and the forged-Control test added. Contract asks: org/reports/CON-02-requests.md (kabir section).
